scope: Full unrecorded source and production brief, renderer mechanism, and final polished native still samples listed below. No continuous playback, measured voice or human listening.

assumptions: Runner is an above-ground stem from the strawberry crown, not a sideways root.
Suitable nodes develop daughter roots and leaves. Root water uptake and leaf photosynthesis are explained before independence is inferred.
Established daughter can continue after separation under suitable conditions. Cutting does not create its pre-existing roots.
Supplied rootless bud does not establish present independent growth; this is not a universal claim that cuttings cannot subsequently root.
Asexual classification follows the mechanism and absence of sperm/egg joining. No chromosome, meiosis or mutation prerequisites are introduced.

studentLearningReview.entryKnowledge: Plants have stems, roots and leaves. The lesson supplies their relevant functions before using them.
studentLearningReview.mainQuestion: How can a strawberry runner produce a plant that grows separately?
studentLearningReview.trace: Parent stem extends; bud at suitable node develops roots and leaves; roots take up water and leaves make food in light; established daughter can support itself; separation can follow. Earlier rootless case lacks its own soil-water uptake.
retainedSuccesses: Runner/stem contrast prevents confusing the mechanism with root growth.
Completed painting is identified as a successful later stage rather than animated growth.
Structure functions explain independence rather than merely naming parts.
Early bud task retains attachment, leaves, absent roots and explanation demand without answer labels.
Feedback keeps the early case and bounds its conclusion.
Separate notes hold supports copying after reasoning.

memoryAid.text: Roots and leaves first. Separation later.
memoryAid.status: scientifically sound as the explained strawberry establishment rule
memoryAid.reason: Reminds learners to check resource-supporting structures before assuming present independent growth. Suitable conditions and enough established roots/leaves are supplied; it is not applied to every vegetative propagation method.

references.checked: University extension full page: crown gives rise to runners, roots and leaves; runners root and produce daughter plants.
University extension search passage: daughter plants unable to root cannot become self-sufficient.
Direct horticultural organisation guidance search passage: sever connection after well-rooted new plant forms.
